headline: Granted variances for garages and an addition on six properties; continued one garage variance request to July
summary: The Zoning Board of Appeals heard seven applications for variances and special permits involving garages, an accessory dwelling unit, a home addition, and an accessory building height. The board granted relief in six cases and continued one case to the July 22, 2026 meeting. The board also corrected an error in the April 22, 2026 minutes regarding a continuance date for 12 Tozer Road.
decisions: Granted a Variance at 26 Mason Street to construct a new detached single-car garage with storage above, 5-0.

Granted a Variance at 20 Roundy Street under Section 300-37 D(8) to allow demolition and reconstruction of a nonconforming accessory structure as an accessory dwelling unit, resulting in a rear yard setback encroachment, 5-0.
Granted a continuance of the Matthew Hergott application at 140 Essex Street to the July 22, 2026 meeting, 5-0.
Granted a Variance at 26 Vine Street to build an additional floor on the existing nonconforming two-family house, 5-0.
Granted a Special Permit at 6 Berkeley Avenue to construct and replace an existing garage with a new garage, 5-0.
Granted a Variance at 824 Hale Street from Section 300-34 D(5) to construct a rear addition encroaching into the rear setback, 5-0.
Granted a Variance at 820 Hale Street from Section 300-27 E(3) to allow an accessory building height of 17 feet where 15 feet is allowed, with special conditions tied to the barn, 5-0.
Acknowledged an error in the April 22, 2026 minutes regarding the 12 Tozer Road continuance date, correcting it to June 24, 2026, 4-0.
Approved the request to continue the 12 Tozer Road application to the June 24, 2026 meeting, 4-0.
Tabled approval of the April 22, 2026 meeting minutes to the June 24, 2026 meeting, 4-0.
plain_text:
CITY of BEVERLY
Zoning Board of Appeals
May 27, 2026 at 7:00 pm
These minutes are not a verbatim transcript of the public hearing of the Board of Appeals.  
Reviews of these Minutes or outcome of the public hearing should include an examination of the 
Board’s decision for that hearing.  
Members Present: Will Cosmas, Chairperson, Michael Barone, Cory Farinella, 
Laura Meisenhelter and Benjamin Roy
Others Present:     Jim Butler, Building Commissioner
Leanna Harris, Administrative Assistant
Location:       Council Chambers City Hall, 191 Cabot Street, Beverly
Will Cosmas began the meeting at 7pm and introduced the members present.
NEW PUBLIC HEARINGS
Albert Turner
requests a Variance to construct a new detached single-car garage with storage above, in 
accordance with Sections 300-27 E-2, E-3, E-4 of the Beverly Zoning Ordinance.  The property 
is located at 26 Mason Street in the RMD zoning district.  
Bill Nolan (Savoie Nolan) addressed the Board on behalf of the applicant and stated this is their 
third meeting before the Zoning Board. At the last meeting there was a clerical issue that resulted
in having them to resubmit the application.  There is nothing new for them to present tonight. 
They are proposing to build a garage.  The previously proposed ADU has been removed from the
plans.  At the last the meeting they did have quite a few neighbors who provided letters in favor 
that the applicant didn’t submit. Mr. Nolan submitted them to the Board.  Based on feedback 
from the neighbors, the plans were largely changed to be an oversized one car garage with 
storage above. There will be no rear or side windows.  It is gambrel style with one window 
facing the street.  
Mr. Roy asked if the rear abutter submitted a letter in support and Mr. Nolan confirmed.
Mr. Nolan stated the deck has also been removed from the plans and the overall garage height 
has been shrunk a little bit. The owner works on cars and would like the space above for storage.
Mr. Nolan stated the existing garage foundation is smaller than the proposed oversized one car 
garage to accommodate today’s vehicles.
No one spoke in favor or against.
Page 2 of 10
MOTION:  Mr. Roy moved to close the public hearing. 
Ms. Meisenhelter seconded the Motion.
Votes in favor: 5-0 (Cosmas, Farinella, Barone, Meisenhelter, Roy)
Motion carries.
Mr. Cosmas stated the applicant has been very good with following up with neighbors and 
addressing their concerns.  Mr. Cosmas stated he appreciates the applicant’s patience with 
having to come back before the Board.
MOTION:  Mr. Farinella moved to GRANT a Variance at 26 Mason Street to construct 
a new detached single-car garage with storage above, in accordance with Sections 300-27
E-2, E-3, E-4 of the Beverly Zoning Ordinance due to the topography and shape of the lot
creating a hardship, subject to the plans submitted. Mr. Roy seconded the Motion. 
Votes in favor: 5-0 (Cosmas, Farinella, Barone, Meisenhelter, Roy)
Motion carries.
Julianna Newmeyer
requests a Variance under §300-37 D(8) of the Zoning Ordinance to allow the demolition and
reconstruction of a pre-existing, nonconforming accessory structure as an accessory dwelling
unit, resulting in a rear yard setback encroachment. The property is located at 20 Roundy
Street in the RHD Zoning district.
Julianna Newmeyer addressed the Board and introduced her husband, Colin.  Ms. Newmeyer 
stated they are proposing to demolish an existing detached garage and replace it with an attached 
2-car garage with a small Accessory Dwelling Unit above it.  The existing garage is small and 
already nonconforming in relation to the side and rear setbacks.  The proposed garage would be 
moved to comply with the 10’ side setback.  Ms. Newmeyer stated the relief they are requesting 
tonight is for the rear setback.  It would be encroaching approximately 7’ into the 20’ required 
setback due to the lot configuration and the location of the existing structures.  They are 
eliminating the side nonconformity.  Ms. Newmeyer stated that they are not dramatically 
increasing the overall footprint and the request is consistent with the Commonwealth’s ADU 
guidelines.
Mr. Cosmas asked if there is a better copy of the Site Plan than what was submitted.  The 
applicant provided a copy and Mr. Cosmas shared it with the Board members.
Mr. Cosmas asked for confirmation that they are requesting to demolish an existing structure on 
the property and replace it with another structure that would have an ADU and would encroach 
on the rear setback.  The applicants confirmed.  Mr. Cosmas asked if the existing structure is 
falling down and Mr. Newmeyer stated its not but it is in disrepair, it’s from the 1800s.
Mr. Barone if they spoke with the neighbor behind them.  Ms. Newmeyer stated they sent him a 
letter but they did not hear back.
Page 3 of 10
Mr. Barone stated he appreciates that they are getting rid of the nonconforming setback. His 
biggest concern is the overall height with the ADU on top.  They are already close to the lot line. 
Mr. Barone stated they are in a unique position due to the unique position of the lot.
Mike Orlando, 18 Roundy Street stated he is a new Beverly resident as of March. He has been 
exchanging emails with the applicant regarding the project they are proposing. Mr. Orlando
stated he is on board with the project and he would like to see it move forward.
MOTION: Mr. Roy moved to close the public hearing.  
Mr. Farinella seconded the Motion.
Votes in favor: 5-0 (Cosmas, Farinella, Barone, Meisenhelter, Roy)
Motion carries.
Mr. Barone asked if they explored putting the garage where the existing structure is.  Mr. 
Newmeyer stated anywhere they tried to put it with the site conditions they were going to not be 
in compliance with the setbacks.
Mr. Cosmas asked for clarification that in the application they stated they aren’t finished with the
plans yet because they are waiting for approval before investing the funds to get a complete 
rendering.  Mr. Cosmas stated the location specified on the Site Plan has to remain the same.  If 
there are any changes they would need to come back before the Board.
Mr. Roy asked what side the ADUs windows would be facing.  Mr. Newmeyer stated there 
would be none on the Roundy Street side, they are facing their house.
MOTION: Mr. Roy moved to GRANT a Variance at 20 Roundy Street under §300-37 D(8) of 
the Zoning Ordinance to allow the demolition and reconstruction of a pre-existing, 
nonconforming accessory structure as an accessory dwelling unit, resulting in a rear yard setback
encroachment, due to the shape of the lot and the location of the existing structure creating a 
hardship, subject to the plans submitted.  Ms. Meisenhelter seconded the Motion,
Votes in favor: 5-0 (Cosmas, Farinella, Barone, Meisenhelter, Roy)
Motion carries.
Matthew Hergott
requests a Variance from Section 300-27 E-2, 3, and 4 of the Beverly Zoning Ordinance to raze 
and reconstruct a pre-existing nonconforming detached garage. The applicant seeks relief from 
the rear-yard setback and the maximum height requirements for accessory structures to allow for 
the construction of a two-story garage on the existing footprint. The proposed structure will 
maintain nonconforming rear-yard setbacks of approximately 2.7 feet to 2.8 feet along the 
property boundary. The project includes a height increase to accommodate a second-story home 
office. The property is located at 140 Essex Street in the R10 Zoning District.
Mr. and Mrs. Hergott addressed the Board and stated they are seeking a Variance to rebuild their 
detached garage on the existing footprint.  Last summer the garage was damaged in a fluke 
microburst storm when their neighbor’s tree fell on it. It would cost more to repair the garage
Page 4 of 10
than to rebuild it.  Ms. Hergott state they want to build up and add a second floor for their office 
and a half bathroom.  
Mr. Butler stated this is not a home business, they just work from home. There are no clients 
coming to the home. It is just a home office.
Mr. Cosmas asked how tall the structure would be.  Mr. Butler stated on the elevation plans it 
shows 23.0’ to the peak.
Ms. Hergott stated two abutters behind them are 3-story, 2-family homes.
Mr. Barone asked if there is a particular reason why they are rebuilding it in the existing location 
and not moving it forward to make it conforming.  Mr. Hergott stated it is currently a cinder 
block foundation and there is no telling how far it goes down or if it is filled with concrete.   Ms. 
Hergott stated this house was a major fixer upper and they have spent a lot of money to rebuild 
the patio.  They like the open flow from the garage to the patio.  Ms. Hergott stated it would take 
a lot of time and money to rebuild that space. 
Mr. Barone stated he is having difficulty finding what the hardship is.  There are certain criteria 
that has to be met for the Board to grant a Variance.  Mr. Barone stated his concern is that they 
have plenty of space to relocate the garage, more so since they aren’t using the existing 
foundation. It could be made to be conforming in both dimensional requirements.  The existing 
location is 3’ off the lot line when they do have adequate space to build it elsewhere on the lot.
No one spoke in favor or against.
Ms. Hergott stated they have spoken with their neighbors and there are no concerns there.
Mr. Cosmas stated the applicants do have a decent sized lot and there are places the garage could
go. Ms. Hergott stated they would have to take trees down and move gardens and reconstruct 
their driveway if they were to move it to the open green space.
Mr. Barone stated he is concerned that the hardship is self-created.   The applicants have the 
ability to address two of the three variances simply by moving the location.  Mr. Barone stated 
the hardship is tied to the lot.
MOTION:  Mr. Farinella moved to close the public hearing.
Mr. Barone seconded the Motion. 
Votes in favor: 5-0 (Cosmas, Farinella, Barone, Meisenhelter, Roy)
Motion carries.
Mr. Cosmas read the Variance requirements from the Beverly Zoning Ordinance.
Ms. Meisenhelter stated it’s a double lot which adds to the difficulty. Meisenhelter stated to her 
what they are proposing is creating the least amount of change to the lot and the neighborhood.
Page 5 of 10
Mr. Cosmas reviewed the options available to the applicants as far as moving forward for a vote 
tonight.
The applicants requested a continuance to the July meeting.
MOTION:  Mr. Barone moved to GRANT a continuance to the July 22, 2026 meeting.  
Mr. Roy seconded the Motion.
Votes in favor: 5-0 (Cosmas, Farinella, Barone, Meisenhelter, Roy)
Motion carries.
Alexander & Femino o/b/o Richard Healey
requests a Variance to build an additional floor on the existing legally nonconforming two 
family house to enlarge the one bedroom second floor unit.  The additional floor will be built 
within the footprint of the existing house and the resulting height of the house as renovated will 
be 5 feet less than what is allowed in this zoning district.  The property is located at 26 Vine 
Street in the R10 zoning district.
Tom Alexander, Esq.  (Alexander & Femino) addressed the Board on behalf of the applicant and 
stated it is a 2-family dwelling, the first floor has one bedroom and the second floor also has one 
bedroom.  The house is owned and occupied on the second floor by Richard Healey.  Mr. 
Healey’s parents live on the first floor.  Atty. Alexander stated according to the Assessor’s 
records the house was built in 1905.  The lot is really narrow, it is 32.8’ in the front and 39.2’ in 
the rear.  The building on site takes up most of the lot.  The lot size area is 1,616 sq. ft. The 
existing height is 23’ to the peak.  The applicant is looking to add a floor to the property so he 
can expand the second floor to a 3-bedroom unit.  The increase in height would be 7’ which is 
still below the height restriction in this zone.  The maximum heigh allowed is 35’.  The third 
floor addition would be within the existing footprint, its set in a little bit.  In the rear its 11.8’ 
within the footprint and on the side it is 1.1’ within the footprint.  The front its 2.8’ within the 
footprint.  This house abuts Beverly Farms Public Library on the left and it abuts the Beverly 
Fire Department in the rear.
Atty. Alexander stated they are looking for a Variance due to the shape of the narrow lot and also 
the building location is a limiting factor.  In that neighborhood there are eight houses that are 
already 3-stories.
Atty. Alexander distributed a map and signed petition from neighbors who have signed in favor.
Mr. Cosmas asked if the proposal is increasing the nonconformity and Atty. Alexander stated it is
not. The building volume is being increased, but the footprint is not.
Mr. Barone asked what the total increase in square footage would be.   Atty. Alexander stated it 
is approximately 50%.  The architect stated it is less than 50% because the addition is recessed 
from the footprint.
Page 6 of 10
Mr. McGinnis, 23 Vine Street stated he lives across the street and he doesn’t have an issue with 
this proposal.  The applicant is a good neighbor.
MOTION:  Mr. Roy move to close the public hearing.
Ms. Meisenhelter seconded the Motion.
Votes in favor: 5-0 (Cosmas, Farinella, Barone, Meisenhelter, Roy)
Motion carries.
Mr. Cosmas stated this requests better aligns with a Variance than other applications they have 
heard.  
MOTION:  Mr. Barone moved to GRANT a Variance at 26 Vine Street to build an 
additional floor on the existing legally nonconforming two family house to enlarge the 
one bedroom second floor unit.  The additional floor will be built within the footprint of 
the existing house and the resulting height of the house as renovated will be 5 feet less 
than what is allowed in this zoning district based on the narrow lot and the position of the
existing structure on the lot creating a hardship, subject to the plans submitted.  
Mr. Farinella seconded the Motion.
Votes in favor: 5-0 (Cosmas, Farinella, Barone, Meisenhelter, Roy)
Motion carries.
Timothy Harney
requests a Special Permit to construct and replace existing garage with new garage. The 
property is located at 6 Berkeley Avenue in the R10 zoning district.
Mr. Roy discussed recusing himself.
Tim Harney addressed the Board and stated they are looking to rebuild a garage on the same 
footprint.  Mr. Harney stated it is currently being held up by what is in it.
No one spoke in favor or against.
MOTION:  Mr. Barone moved to close the public hearing. 
Mr. Roy seconded the Motion.
Votes in favor: 5-0 (Cosmas, Farinella, Barone, Meisenhelter, Roy)
Motion carries.
Mr. Harney submitted letters in favor from abutters.
Mr. Barone stated this request is straight forward, it makes a lot of sense. It’s just going to be 
nicer and newer.  Mr. Cosmas stated he agrees that it’s a reasonable request.
Page 7 of 10
MOTION:  Mr. Barone moved to GRANT a Special Permit at 6 Berkeley Avenue to 
construct and replace existing garage with new garage, subject to the plans submitted.  
Mr. Cosmas seconded the Motion.
Votes in favor: 5-0 (Cosmas, Farinella, Barone, Meisenhelter, Roy)
Motion carries.
824 Hale Street LLC
requests a Variance from Section 300-34 D(5) to construct a rear addition onto an existing
nonconforming dwelling encroaching into the rear setback. The property is located at 824 Hale
Street in the R10 zoning district.
John Harden (Olson Lewis & Architects) addressed the Board on behalf of Nic and Whitney 
Savignano and stated this is an exciting little project.  It has turned into something that is pretty 
special in many ways.  Mr. Harden stated they had a great meeting with the Historic Commission
and documentation has been submitted.
The two houses at 820 Hale Street and 824 Hale Street are very close together on one lot.
The applicants would like to retain as much of the original house. They are seeking to remove 
the back portion of the home and reconstruct in a way that is more 21st century and has better 
flow within the house. 
The applicants are before the Board today to request a Variance because it is a pre-existing 
nonconforming structure. 
Mr. Harden reviewed the plans. 824 Hale Street is situated awkwardly on the site. It is 
encroaching into the front and rear setbacks. This building was constructed long before zoning or
before anything else was there. It faces exactly south which historically is how houses were built.
  The goal is to update the house but to also make the back area and garage functional.  Several 
drawings were submitted. Mr. Harden reviewed the site plan for the 824 Hale Street property.  
Mr. Harden stated that they did learn from the Historic Commission that the house was built in 
1701. Mr. Harden reviewed the different structures on the site and the order in which they were 
built.  They believe sometime in the 1950s the rear piece was built.  In the Historical 
Commission meeting the applicant proposed that they keep the front pieces but demolish the rear
piece and create a more modern addition.   The barn is currently disconnected, it is located in the 
upper left corner where at some point a screen porch was added.  The porch doesn’t have much 
value but the barn is historic so they are proposing to move the barn to the adjacent property at 
820 Hale Street. This would also provide more room to do the project while maintaining a 
historic piece in a relatively close location.  This is what triggered the second application for 820 
Hale Street.
Ms. Meisenhelter asked what the reason is that the barn can’t stay at the existing location.  Mr. 
Harden stated their addition will sit in that approximate location.  Ms. Meisenhelter asked what 
the date of the barn is. Mr. Harden stated the barn is old, it has been reenforced over the years.  
The wood is soft cut so it is older than this century.
Page 8 of 10
Mr. Harden stated they are sort of filling in what will be the new two car garage and the oldest 
part of the existing house.  There will be a new kitchen, dining area, laundry and access to the 
yard.  The old beams and joints will be worked with.  There are a bunch of bedrooms so 
hopefully a young family will grow up in this house. Both of the front and rear stairs are unsafe 
so new stairs are in the plans. The master suite will be on the second floor.  There is a third floor 
in the oldest part of the house but they don’t expect to do much with that.  
Mr. Harden reviewed the elevations and views from each side.
Mr. Harden stated they are using the back corner of the porch as a starting point so the addition 
will be no closer than what currently exists.
Mr. Cosmas asked if the rear setback will be the same as the screened porch that is being 
removed. Mr. Butler confirmed. Mr. Harden also confirmed and stated it is encroaching 4.3’ into 
the setback.
Mr. Barone stated the plans are very commendable, they are preserving the history of the site.  
Mr. Barone stated he greatly appreciates that they aren’t going any further than what the current 
setbacks are.  
Mr. Roy stated it is a very thoughtful plan.
Ms. Meisenhelter stated she is so happy they are maintaining so much of the history.
No one spoke in favor or against.
Letters in favor were submitted.
MOTION: Mr. Farinella moved to close the public hearing. 
Ms. Meisenhelter seconded the Motion.
Votes in favor: 5-0 (Cosmas, Farinella, Barone, Meisenhelter, Roy)
Motion carries.
MOTION: Mr. Barone moved to GRANT a Variance at 824 Hale Street from Section 
300-34 D(5) to construct a rear addition onto an existing nonconforming dwelling 
encroaching into the rear setback due to the size of the lot and the existing structures on 
the lot creating a hardship, subject to the plans submitted. 
Mr. Cosmas seconded the Motion.
Votes in favor: 5-0 (Cosmas, Farinella, Barone, Meisenhelter, Roy)
Motion carries.
820 Hale Street Realty Trust
requests a Variance to from Section 300-27, E (3) to allow for an accessory building height of
16.94’ where 15.2’ is allowed. The property is located at 820 Hale Street in the R10 zoning
district.
Page 9 of 10
Mr. Cosmas noted that the properties at 820 Hale Street and 824 Hale Street are owned by 
different entities but related owners.  There are no merger issues for zoning purposes. 
Mr. Harden stated in the rear of the property is a dogleg shape that extends behind 824 Hale 
Street. In that dogleg shape is a pool with a patio around it and a pergola that sits at the right 
hand end of the pool.  The historic barn could likely be deconstructed and passed through the 
wall of arborvitaes and reconstructed on the other side taking the place of the pergola.  There 
would be a small bathroom addition to the side of the barn.
Mr. Harden stated the height for an accessory structure is calculated as one half the distance to 
the property line which would allow for the barn to be 15.2’ high.  The original height of the barn
is 17’ high so they are requesting a 1.8’ height variance.  They would like to keep the barn the 
size that it is. 
Mr. Butler stated he drove by the property, it is well hidden.
Mr. Barone stated that he would be comfortable conditioning this approval that if for some 
reason they determine that the barn cannot be used or reconstructed that any other structure 
going in there would have to be reviewed by the Zoning Board.
No one spoke in favor or against.
MOTION:  Ms. Meisenhelter moved to close the public hearing. 
Mr. Farinella seconded the Motion.
Votes in favor: 5-0 (Cosmas, Farinella, Barone, Meisenhelter, Roy)
Motion carries.
Mr. Cosmas stated he likes that proposed condition to the Variance that to the extent moving the 
barn is not feasible, there cannot be another structure built there without further review from this 
Board.
MOTION:  Mr.  Farinella moved to GRANT a Variance at 820 Hale Street to from Section 300-
27, E (3) to allow for an accessory building height of 17’ where 15’ is allowed.  This Variance 
has special conditions to this particular barn, if this barn were not to be erected the Variance 
would not stand, subject to the plans submitted.  Mr. Barone seconded the Motion.
Votes in favor: 5-0 (Cosmas, Farinella, Barone, Meisenhelter, Roy)
Motion carries.
Will – what was the hardship?
OTHER BUSINESS
A. Approval of April 22, 2026 Meeting Minutes (Cosmas)
Mr. Cosmas stated after reviewing the Minutes he noticed that they stated the applicants for 12 
Tozer Road had submitted a request to continue the application to the May 27, 2026 meeting
Page 10 of 10
where the letter they submitted actually stated the June 24, 2026 meeting.
Mr. Cosmas read into the record the written request received asking to continue their application 
to the June 24, 2026 meeting.
Mr. Barone reviewed the Waiver and Agreement language.
Mr. Cosmas noted that there is an email from the applicant’s attorney to abutters notifying them 
of continuance to the June 24, 2026 meeting.
MOTION:  Ms. Meisenhelter stated the Zoning Board of Appeals acknowledges their 
error in the April 22, 2026 meeting concerning the application for 12 Tozer Road 
requesting a continuance.  The date should have been June 24, 2026 not May 27, 2026.  
Mr. Barone seconded the Motion.
Votes in favor: 4-0 (Cosmas, Farinella, Barone, Meisenhelter)
Motion carries.
MOTION: Ms. Meisenhelter moved to approve the request to continuance the 
application at 12 Tozer Road to the June 24, 2026 meeting
Mr. Cosmas seconded the Motion.
Votes in favor: 4-0 (Cosmas, Farinella, Barone, Meisenhelter)
Motion carries.
MOTION:  Mr. Cosmas moved to table the approval of the Minutes from the April 22, 
2026 meeting to the June 24, 2026 meeting.
Votes in favor: 4-0 (Cosmas, Farinella, Barone, Meisenhelter)
Motion carries.
MOTION: Ms. Meisenhelter moved to adjourn the meeting.  
Mr. Farinella seconded the Motion.
Votes in favor: 5-0 (Cosmas, Farinella, Barone, Meisenhelter, Roy)
Motion carries.
Leanna Harris, Administrative Assistant
        Board of Appeals of the Zoning Ordinance
